rationale: All five follow the same route: slice to a plane when q>k-1, and at the endpoint slice to dimension three, use the weak radial estimate to find a transverse triple, and finish with Loomis-Whitney. They differ mainly in how fully each step is checked and organised. B is the most complete and checkable: it fixes the constants in order (a, ell, b_0, e, theta), proves the wedge and kernel claims (Claims A-D) separately, and gives the Holder step explicitly with the correct power of the total mass. It is somewhat long. E is nearly as rigorous, with numbered kernel estimates and clear sections (setup, rarity of dependent triples, extraction, counting), and its explicit Holder constant is a small plus. A is correct and has the clearest upfront overview. Its Claims A-C are tidy but the Holder step and some constants are only sketched. D is the most economical, but it leaves several routine steps to the reader: the kernel summation, the Holder step and the choice of theta are compressed. C cites equations (ang:direction-pair-kernel) and (ang:point-slice-total) that are neither defined nor provided in the context, and it has no explicit overview or step headings. That leaves a gap in the transfer bound and weakens its structure.
